title.narrative: Sustainable Low-Carbon Transportation Strategy in Oman

description.narrative: In February 2021, UNIDO was contacted by the National Ozone Unit of the Sultanate of Oman in regard to partnering together to develop projects focussing on climate change issues. In a subsequent meeting between UNIDO, the Directorate General of Meteorology, Ministry of Environment and Climate Affairs (MECA) and Sultan Qaboos University, it was jointly decided that UNIDO would develop a GCF readiness proposal on low carbon transportation strategy in Oman to be submitted to the GCF in June 2021. A brief summary of the project proposal can be found below: Oman#s transportation sector consumes roughly a three-quarters of total national petroleum products in the country. The transport sector is projected to grow robustly over the coming decades. Unless there is a major shift in the current patterns of energy use, which is unlikely, projections show continued growth in Oman#s transportation sector energy use at 10% per year, with energy use and CO2 emissions projected to grow by 112% over 2015 level by 2030. Emission from the transport sector represents the fastest-growing source of GHG emissions for the period 2000-2015, by nearly 770 times from 1.574 Mt CO2e in 2000 to 13.696 Mt CO2e in 2015 or 14.5% per year.
